hints: Let a square root be $x+iy$, square it, and compare real and imaginary parts.
Use $x^2-y^2=-1$ and $2xy=-4\sqrt5$ to eliminate one variable and obtain the required quartic.
Solve the quartic through a quadratic in $x^2$ or $y^2$, using $xy<0$ to pair the signs.
State the two complex roots as opposites in exact Cartesian form and verify by squaring.
walkthrough:
Let the square root be $z = x + \mathrm{i}y$, where $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$:
$$(x + \mathrm{i}y)^2 = -1 - 4\sqrt{5}\,\mathrm{i}$$
$$x^2 + 2\mathrm{i}xy - y^2 = -1 - 4\sqrt{5}\,\mathrm{i}$$
$$(x^2 - y^2) + 2xy\,\mathrm{i} = -1 - 4\sqrt{5}\,\mathrm{i}$$

Equate real and imaginary parts:
$$x^2 - y^2 = -1 \quad \text{--- (1)}$$
$$2xy = -4\sqrt{5} \implies y = -\dfrac{2\sqrt{5}}{x} \quad \text{--- (2)}$$

Substitute equation (2) into equation (1) to eliminate $y$:
$$x^2 - \left(-\dfrac{2\sqrt{5}}{x}\right)^2 = -1$$
$$x^2 - \dfrac{4 \times 5}{x^2} = -1$$
$$x^2 - \dfrac{20}{x^2} = -1$$

Multiply throughout by $x^2$ and rearrange into a quadratic in $x^2$:
$$(x^2)^2 - 20 = -x^2$$
$$(x^2)^2 + x^2 - 20 = 0$$

Factor the quadratic in $x^2$:
$$(x^2 + 5)(x^2 - 4) = 0$$
$$\text{Since } x \in \mathbb{R}, \; x^2 \geqslant 0, \text{ so } x^2 + 5 \neq 0.$$
$$x^2 = 4 \implies x = 2 \quad \text{or} \quad x = -2$$

Find the corresponding values of $y$ using $y = -\dfrac{2\sqrt{5}}{x}$:
$$\text{When } x = 2: \quad y = -\dfrac{2\sqrt{5}}{2} = -\sqrt{5} \implies z = 2 - \sqrt{5}\,\mathrm{i}$$
$$\text{When } x = -2: \quad y = -\dfrac{2\sqrt{5}}{-2} = \sqrt{5} \implies z = -2 + \sqrt{5}\,\mathrm{i}$$

State the square roots as a paired expression:
$$\pm(2 - \sqrt{5}\,\mathrm{i})$$
